title: Modulating the Noradrenergic Pathway from Locus Coeruleus to Heart in Mouse Models
author: Xu, Wang, et al.
materials: This section describes the preparation and storage methods of reagents required for the experiment.5.For anesthetization: dissolve 3.5 g chloral hydrate in 100 mL sterilized 0.9% saline to make 3.5% chloral hydrate solution.Note: Store the chloral hydrate (3.5%) at room temperature (RT, 15°C–25°C) for up to 1 month.6.According to the corresponding drug concentration, dissolve atomoxetine, esmolol and N-(2-chloroethyl)-N-ethyl-2-bromobenzylamin hydrochloride (DSP-4) in 0.9% saline.Note: Compound the drug when it is used, avoid storage for more than 3 h and do not leave it at 21°C–26°C for too long.7.Take out rAAV-DBH-GCaMP6m-WPRE-hGH pA virus, and put it on the ice immediately before viral loading and wrap it in tinfoil to protect it from light.

steps.title: Prepare all reagents
steps.instruction: Make a 3.5% chloral hydrate solution by dissolving 3.5 g chloral hydrate in 100 mL sterile 0.9 % saline; store at room temperature (15 °C–25 °C) for up to 1 month. Dissolve atomoxetine, esmolol and DSP‑4 each in 0.9 % saline to the required concentrations immediately before use, keep the solutions for no longer than 3 h and avoid keeping them at 21 °C–26 °C. Retrieve the rAAV‑DBH‑GCaMP6m‑WPRE‑hGH pA virus, keep it on ice and wrap in foil to protect from light.

steps.title: Set up stereotaxic injection system
steps.instruction: Connect a 10 µL gauge needle (for virus injection) to the micro‑infusion pump, assemble the stereotaxic instrument and dental drill, and verify needle air‑tightness by checking for a droplet at the tip before loading virus.

steps.title: Anesthetize and position mouse
steps.instruction: Turn on a heating pad to maintain the mouse at 37 °C. Weigh the mouse and calculate the chloral hydrate dose (15 g DBA/1 male: 0.23 mL of 3.5 % solution, i.e., 15 mL/kg). Inject the calculated volume intraperitoneally, wait 5–10 min and assess responsiveness to a noxious stimulus. If anesthesia is insufficient after 10 min, give an additional 0.05 mL of 3.5 % chloral hydrate.

steps.title: Prepare surgical site and implant fibers
steps.instruction: Fix the mouse head in the stereotaxic frame using ear bars and secure the front teeth on the tooth bar. Apply erythromycin eye ointment to the eyes and cover with sterile cotton balls. Remove the scalp skin, wipe the skull with an alcohol‑soaked cotton ball, then clean the bone seam with a hydrogen‑peroxide‑soaked cotton ball to expose bregma and lambda. Using the dental drill, thin the skull at the locus coeruleus coordinates on both hemispheres. Load the virus into the gauge needle and implant an optical fiber into each LC site. Secure the fibers with dental cement.

substeps.instruction: Fix head with ear bars and tooth bar.
Apply erythromycin ointment and cover eyes.
Remove scalp and clean skull with alcohol.
Drill at LC coordinates on both sides.

description: In the DBA/1 mouse model, both cardiac and respiratory functions are suppressed simultaneously during the induction of S-IRA and SUDEP, suggesting that the autonomic nervous system, including the sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems, is involved in S-IRA and SUDEP.2 Improving the efficiency of synaptic transmission of NE in the brain has been shown to effectively reduce the incidence of SUDEP.3,4 Thus, we hypothesize that the interaction between noradrenergic neurons in the LC and β1-AR on cardiomyocytes plays a key role in the regulation of SUDEP, which could be a potential target for SUDEP prevention and provide a new perspective for elucidating the pathogenesis of SUDEP. The approach is mainly based on calcium signaling, ECG recordings and ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) to illustrate the role of the brain-heart axis in the occurrence of SUDEP.
